info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package source is the registry of a person's linked Hanzo Dev sources (HIP-1350, slice 1): link, list, read, revoke and heartbeat, served at /v1/sources and as the ZAP service source.v1 from the same typed ops.

get.summary: Returns the signed-in person's own active sources, newest heartbeat first, each with its online state and provider state.
get.description:
Returns the signed-in person's own active sources, newest
heartbeat first, each with its online state and provider state. There is no
read of another person's sources: not for an org admin, not for a SuperAdmin.

post.summary: Links this install to the signed-in person, or refreshes the install that already holds the same device key and answers with its existing id.
post.description:
Links this install to the signed-in person, or refreshes the install that
already holds the same device key and answers with its existing id. The person
and org come from the validated token and never from the body; a machine token
is refused. A person holds at most 25 active sources and may link 10 new ones
an hour.

get.summary: Returns the signed-in person's own provider accounts with the route class each may run under: the keys they sealed into KMS, and the logins their linked sources report.
get.description:
Returns the signed-in person's own provider accounts with the route
class each may run under: the keys they sealed into KMS, and the logins their
linked sources report. A key shows a label and fingerprint, never its value. A
login is read-only here and disappears when its source stops reporting it.

post.summary: Seals a provider API key into KMS and records a reference to it.
post.description:
Seals a provider API key into KMS and records a reference to it.
KMS keeps the value at kms://orgs/<org>/users/<person>/providers/<provider>/<id>;
the row keeps that path, the label and a fingerprint, and nothing else. The value
is in no response, log, trace or audit field, and not even the owner can read it
back: the gateway resolves it at call time. Only `kind: "key"` is accepted, for a
provider that takes a key.

delete.summary: Removes one of the signed-in person's own provider keys.
delete.description:
Removes one of the signed-in person's own provider keys. KMS is
asked to delete the secret first and the row goes only after it has; if KMS
cannot, the answer is 502 and the account stays. Another person's id is 404. A
login cannot be deleted here: it goes when the person logs out on its source.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the account, from the path.

get.summary: Totals the signed-in person's own reported usage by source, provider, model, day or user between two days, with their latest snapshot per source and provider.
get.description:
Totals the signed-in person's own reported usage by source,
provider, model, day or user between two days, with their latest snapshot per
source and provider. An org admin asking by=user gets every person's totals in
the org (key is the person's subject) and nothing else of theirs: no source,
snapshot, plan or label of another person is readable, and a SuperAdmin has no
extra read. For anyone else by=user is their own single row.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: From is the first day included, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: To is the last day included, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

delete.summary: Unlinks one of the signed-in person's own sources and drops its provider state, so nothing routes through it.
delete.description:
Unlinks one of the signed-in person's own sources and drops its
provider state, so nothing routes through it. The act is audited. The source's
next heartbeat answers 410 and it forgets the link. Revoking twice is the same
answer as once.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the source, from the path.

get.summary: Returns one of the signed-in person's own sources, including a revoked one, whose state reads `revoked`.
get.description:
Returns one of the signed-in person's own sources, including a
revoked one, whose state reads `revoked`. Another person's id and an unknown id
answer the same 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the source, from the path.

post.summary: Looks up where a session may run on one of the caller's own linked desktops and takes the lease for it; it is the lookup the /v1/dev execution field calls, and frames then flow from the browser to the desktop, not through cloud.
post.description:
Looks up where a session may run on one of the caller's own linked
desktops and takes the lease for it; it is the lookup the /v1/dev execution field
calls, and frames then flow from the browser to the desktop, not through cloud. It
grants only when the caller owns the source (another person's is 404, with no
admin or SuperAdmin path), the source is not revoked, is a desktop with a ZAP
endpoint and a heartbeat in the last 90 seconds, the login instance is `ready`
and shared, the provider's classes include `desktop`, and no live lease holds the
instance (one run per login at a time, 15 minutes). Every grant and refusal is
audited. A refusal carries `code`: revoked (410), class (403), no_endpoint,
offline, not_ready, not_shared, busy (409).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the source, from the path.

delete.summary: Ends a run's hold on a login instance, so the next run can start before the lease lapses.
delete.description:
Ends a run's hold on a login instance, so the next run can start
before the lease lapses. Only the person who holds the lease can release it; any
other lease or source is 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the source, from the path.

parameters.name: lease
parameters.description: Lease is the lease to release, from the path.

post.summary: Records that a source is alive and what its providers can do, and answers the interval and usage level.
post.description:
Records that a source is alive and what its providers can do, and
answers the interval and usage level. The beat is signed by the source's device
key, so a stolen token alone cannot impersonate it: a bad or missing signature is
401. A revoked source is answered 410 and should forget the link. A source is
online for 90 seconds after a beat; beats closer than 10 seconds are refused 429.
Providers are state only and carry no token, email or key material.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the source, from the path.

post.summary: usage is the raw handler: the signature covers the exact body bytes and rides in a header, neither of which a typed op can see.
post.description:
usage is the raw handler: the signature covers the exact body bytes and rides in
a header, neither of which a typed op can see.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

classes.description:
Classes are where it may run: `key`, `desktop` and `local`, from the provider
policy. A browser source's logins are `local` only.

created.description: Created is when the key was sealed, or the login's source was linked, RFC 3339 UTC.

fingerprint.description: Fingerprint is the first 8 hex digits of sha256 of a key's value. Keys only.

id.description: ID is the account id. A login's is `<source id>:<instance>`.

instance.description: Instance is the login's instance id on that source. Logins only.

label.description: Label is the name the person gave a key, or the instance of a login.

plan.description: Plan is a login's plan label. Logins only.

provider.description: Provider is the provider's catalog name, for example `anthropic`.

shared.description: Shared is whether the person offered this login to their other surfaces. Logins only.

sourceId.description: SourceID is the source that reported a login. Logins only.

state.description: State is a login's `ready`, `needs_login` or `limited`. Logins only.

id.description: ID is the account that was removed.

accounts.description: Accounts are the caller's keys, then the logins their sources report.

kind.description: Kind is `key`. A login cannot be created here: it appears when a source reports it.

label.description: Label names the key, up to 64 characters. Required.

provider.description:
Provider is the provider the key is for, for example `anthropic`. It must be one
that takes a key.

value.description: Value is the key. It is sealed into KMS and appears in no response, log or audit.

arch.description: Arch is the CPU architecture the install reported.

id.description: ID is the source's id, `src_` and 32 hex digits.

kind.description: Kind is `desktop` (an installed Dev app) or `browser` (the Hanzo extension).

last_seen.description: LastSeen is the last accepted heartbeat, RFC 3339 UTC. Absent before the first.

linked_at.description: LinkedAt is when the source was linked, RFC 3339 UTC.

name.description: Name is the label the person gave this install.

os.description: OS is the operating system the install reported.

providers.description: Providers is the provider state from the last heartbeat.

state.description: State is `online` (a heartbeat within 90 seconds), `offline`, or `revoked`.

version.description: Version is the Dev app version, as of the last link or heartbeat.

zap.description:
Zap is the source's reachable ZAP endpoint. Absent when it has none, in
which case it is registered and not routable.

at.description:
At is when the source made the beat, RFC 3339. It must be within five
minutes of the server clock and newer than the last accepted beat.

busy.description: Busy is how many runs the source is executing.

id.description: ID is the source, from the path.

providers.description:
Providers is the state of each provider instance on the source, replacing
the last set. State only; at most 32.

sig.description:
Sig is the ed25519 signature by the device key over the beat, unpadded base64url.
The signed message is `hanzo-source-heartbeat/1`, then one line each (LF
terminated) for id, at, version, zap, busy, and per provider in order
`provider,instance,kind,state,plan,shared` (shared as `true` or `false`).

version.description: Version is the Dev app version now.

zap.description: Zap is the source's reachable ZAP endpoint now. Empty clears it.

interval.description: Interval is the heartbeat period in seconds.

level.description: Level is the usage level the person chose.

revoked.description: Revoked is false: a revoked source is answered 410 instead.

id.description: ID is the source, from the path.

instance.description: Instance is the login's instance id on the source, for example `claude-1`.

provider.description: Provider is the provider the login is for, for example `claude`.

arch.description: Arch is the CPU architecture, for example `arm64`. Required, up to 64 characters.

key.description:
Key is the install's own ed25519 public device key, 32 bytes as unpadded
base64url. Heartbeats are signed with its private half. Required.

kind.description:
Kind is `desktop` or `browser`. Required, and fixed once linked: relinking the
same key with another kind is a 409.

name.description: Name is the label to show for this install, up to 128 characters. Required.

os.description: OS is the operating system, for example `darwin`. Required, up to 64 characters.

version.description: Version is the Dev app version. Required, up to 64 characters.

zap.description:
Zap is the install's reachable ZAP endpoint, an https or wss URL up to 512
characters. Optional: without it the source is registered and not routable.

id.description: ID is the source's id. Relinking the same device key returns the same id.

interval.description: Interval is the heartbeat period in seconds.

level.description: Level is the usage level the person chose: `metadata`.

sources.description: Sources is every active source of the caller, newest heartbeat first.

instance.description: Instance names this login or key on the source, for example `claude-1`.

kind.description: Kind is `login` (a subscription session that stays on the source) or `key`.

plan.description: Plan is the plan label the provider reports, for example `max`. May be empty.

provider.description: Provider is the provider's catalog name, for example `claude`.

shared.description:
Shared is the person's local choice to offer this login to their other surfaces
(default off). It is reported, never decided here.

lease.description: Lease is the lease that was released.

id.description: ID is the source that was revoked.

expires.description: Expires is when the lease lapses by itself, RFC 3339 UTC. 15 minutes from the grant.

instance.description: Instance is the login instance granted.

lease.description: Lease is the hold on the instance for one run; release it when the run ends.

zap.description: Zap is the source's ZAP endpoint, used exactly as given by the machine runtime.

key.description: Key is the source id, provider, model, day (YYYY-MM-DD) or user subject the row groups by.

rows.description: Rows are the totals per key.

snapshots.description: Snapshots are the caller's own latest snapshot per source and provider.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
